::: {.cite-bar .domain-intelligence}
[In force]{.status .status-in-force} [Pub. L. 81-110]{.cite} [63 Stat. 208]{.cite} [50 U.S.C. 3501-3523]{.cite}
:::

Gave the CIA the administrative tools to operate in secret: authority to spend money without the usual accounting rules, to withhold information about its staff and structure, and to procure and transfer funds confidentially.

## Key provisions

- Sec. 5: transfer and receipt of funds from other agencies without regard to normal appropriations limits.
- Sec. 6: exemption from laws requiring disclosure of the agency's organization, functions, names, titles, salaries, or staff numbers.
- Sec. 8: spending on confidential or emergency objects accounted for solely on the Director's certificate.

## Why it matters

Where the [National Security Act](nsa-1947.qmd) created the agency, this act made clandestine work administratively possible. It is also the root of the 'black budget' question, since it permits intelligence funds to be hidden inside other appropriations.

## Current status

In force as amended.
